papers.title: ReDiffNet: Differential RGB-Infrared Learning for Low-Light UAV Oriented Vehicle Detection
papers.reason: RGB-infrared low-light vehicle detection；将RGB-红外两模态可靠性选择与差分恢复机制，调整到雷达/视觉或AIS/视觉多传感器船舶检测：输入改为雷达点云或AIS
papers.abstract: Low-light UAV-based RGB-infrared oriented small-vehicle detection is important for nighttime traffic monitoring, emergency response, and urban inspection. Illumination variations, headlight glare, local shadows, and thermal-response degradation cause spatially varying modality reliability, while the small visual extent of vehicles further weakens boundaries, orientation cues, and thermal responses. Accordingly, selecting trustworthy observations based on local modality reliability while further exploiting complementary discriminative information in regions with ambiguous modality preference is key to constructing effective multimodal representations. Based on this insight, we propose ReDiffNet, a reliability-conditioned differential representation network in which modality reliability guides both evidence selection and complementary recovery. Specifically, degradation-aware reliability learning estimates relative spatial reliability, uncertainty-guided differential recovery exploits cross-modal differences to recover complementary cues in ambiguous regions, and reliability-conditioned reconstruction integrates retained and recovered evidence into a unified representation. ReDiffNet achieves 85.3% and 73.9% mAP50 on DroneVehicle and VEDAI, respectively, supporting its effectiveness.

papers.title: LiG-DETR: Local-in-Global Reassembly in Latent Space for Aerial Object Detection
papers.reason: object_detection；将全局-局部特征重组与联合解码结构迁移到船舶检测：输入为海上图像，保留共享编码器提取全局和局部放大特征，按空间位置重组局部特征后由DETR解码器联合解码，以提升小尺度
papers.abstract: Aerial object detection faces substantial scale and density variations. Small objects are easily degraded by downsampling and feature compression, while medium and large objects require sufficient global context. Existing methods mainly follow two paradigms: image slicing provides clearer local evidence but relies on independent crop-level prediction and post-processing, whereas feature- and query-level optimization preserves unified inference but operates on already compressed full-image representations, limiting recovery of fine-grained information. This raises a key question: can aerial detection directly acquire high-fidelity local evidence before feature degradation and integrate it into a unified end-to-end framework? To this end, we propose LiG-DETR, an Efficient Global-Local Reassembly framework that reformulates image slicing as high-fidelity local feature acquisition. A shared encoder extracts global and locally magnified features, which are projected into the detector feature space. The projected local features are reassembled according to their original spatial locations to form a globally aligned local feature level, and a single DETR decoder jointly decodes global and local features. To reduce redundant computation, Context-Preserved Selective Reassembly focuses high-resolution encoding on informative regions while preserving a dense feature layout, and Density-Aware Adaptive Query Allocation adapts the decoder query budget using encoder proposal scores. Experiments show substantial gains on small and medium objects while retaining strong large-object performance, with favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-offs and improved cross-domain generalization. The code will be released.

papers.title: TartanMatch: Towards Universal Dense Correspondence Across Modalities
papers.reason: cross_modal_matching；将轻量模态适配模块用于视觉–AIS或Radar–AIS跨模态匹配：保留共享匹配主干，为AIS/雷达增加模态适配层；若无配对真值，可用仿真或按轨迹关联构造合成对
papers.abstract: Robotic platforms combine multi-modal sensors to operate across diverse conditions, but most dense correspondence methods are limited to RGB-RGB or a small set of modality pairs. Training a model for each modality pair scales poorly with the number of sensors and forgoes potential positive transfer across modality pairs. We introduce TartanMatch, a unified model for dense correspondence across all 25 ordered pairs among RGB, event, thermal, depth, and projected LiDAR. TartanMatch adapts an RGB-pretrained correspondence model to all modality pairs within one shared network using lightweight modality adaptation and a mixture of real and synthetic data. On zero-shot real-world benchmarks, TartanMatch reduces Endpoint Error (EPE) over the strongest baselines by 61.9% for cross-modal matching and 49.6% for same-modal matching. We further show that joint training across all modality pairs improves average matching accuracy over pair-specific training, especially on challenging cross-modal pairs. These results demonstrate that a single model achieves broad multi-modal coverage and state-of-the-art matching accuracy.

papers.title: ROSETTA: Rotation Subspace Estimation for Training-free Transmodal Alignment
papers.reason: training-free_transmodal_alignment；将面向LiDAR/相机/热成像/事件跨模态匹配的免训练旋转校准层迁移到视觉–AIS或雷达–AIS跨模态匹配：源域编码器改为船舶视觉
papers.abstract: When a query must be matched against a database built with a different sensor or processed by a different encoder, the independently trained encoders impose distinct coordinate systems on the feature space. No canonical reference frame exists to which all encoders can be aligned, and no single training procedure has fully closed this gap. We show that the relative transformation between any two such systems is a spatially preserving rotation in whitened feature space, whose angular velocity exhibits white-noise characteristics: large in norm, temporally uncorrelated, and unpredictable from the features themselves. However, the cross-covariance between encoder outputs has low effective rank, constraining only a small fraction of the rotation parameters, therefore local alignment is tractable. ROSETTA is a training-free calibration layer that estimates the local rotation via an expectation-maximization procedure, requiring no coobservation at query time. We validate ROSETTA on three public driving datasets spanning LiDAR, camera, thermal, and event modalities in cross-modal, cross-device, cross-representation, and cross-backbone settings, with milliseconds overhead per query.
papers.abstract_zh: 当一个查询必须与一个用不同传感器建立或由不同编码器处理的数据库相匹配时,独立训练的编码器对特征空间强制实施不同的坐标系统. 不存在可以对所有编码器进行对齐的划线参考框架,也没有单一的训练程序完全堵住了这一缺口. 我们显示,任何两个这样的系统之间的相对转变都是在白化的特征空间中保持空间旋转,其角速显示出白噪声的特征:在规范中很大,时间上不相关,从特征本身来看是不可预测的。 然而,编码器产出之间的相互交错有效级别较低,只限制了轮调参数的一小部分,因此是本地的。 对齐 可拖动. ROSETTA 无训练 校准 层,通过期望最大化程序估计本地旋转,在查询时不需要共同观察。 我们确认 ROSETTA 三个公共驾驶数据集 LiDAR, 相机、热能和事件 模态 在 跨模态, 交叉设备, 交叉-表征, 和交叉背骨设置,每次查询为毫秒.

papers.title: Shared Geometry As A Rosetta Stone: Cross-Modal Alignment Without Paired Data
papers.reason: 无配对数据的跨模态对齐；可将两组独立训练嵌入间的正交映射对齐用于视觉–AIS或雷达–AIS跨模态匹配：输入改为视觉检测嵌入与AIS/雷达轨迹嵌入，训练目标改为估计正交对齐映射，结构上可保留几何初始化与
papers.abstract: Multimodal representations enable zero-shot classification and retrieval, but aligning independently trained models usually requires large amounts of paired data. Yet, the Platonic Representation Hypothesis suggests that models trained on different modalities may converge spontaneously toward a shared representation geometry. But then, do we even need paired examples for cross-modal alignment? Remarkably, we show that paired examples are unnecessary for coarse cross-modal alignment. Our simple Wasserstein Procrustes method with a coarse geometric initialization aligns two disjoint embedding sets by estimating a single orthogonal map without seeing any pairs. Across datasets, modalities, and unimodal models, we show that we can consistently align independently trained representations without pairs, and standard geometric alignment metrics accurately predict when this is possible. Nevertheless, we can naturally benefit from paired examples. In the very few-pair regime, our method substantially outperforms existing ones, while staying competitive with pair-based methods with more added examples. Finally, we demonstrate that the resulting alignments can enable text-to-image generation without paired examples. These results show that independently trained models often share enough geometry to establish cross-modal correspondence with little or no paired data.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态 表征 启用 零样本 分类和检索,但调整独立训练的模型通常需要大量的对接数据. 然而,柏拉图 表征 假想表明,模型经过了不同的培训。 模态 可能自发地趋同到共同的 表征 几何来. 但是,我们甚至需要配对的例子 跨模态 对齐? 值得注意的是,我们显示配对的例子对于粗糙是不必要的 跨模态 对齐. 我们简单的Wasserstein Procrustes 方法,用粗几何初始化,通过估计单个正对映图来对准两套脱节嵌入相机,没有看到任何对. 整个数据集, 模态, 和单模式模式,我们显示,我们能够始终如一地将训练有素的 表征 和标准的几何 对齐 精确预测何时可以做到这一点。 然而,我们可以自然地从对等的例子中受益。 在极少数国家体制中,我们的方法大大超过现有的方法,同时与有更多实例的对等方法保持竞争。 最后,我们表明,由此产生的校正可以使文本到图像生成无需配对的例子。 这些结果显示,经过独立培训的模型往往具有足够的几何特征,可以建立 跨模态 对应数据少或没有对齐的函证.

reserve_papers.abstract: Multimodal representations enable zero-shot classification and retrieval, but aligning independently trained models usually requires large amounts of paired data. Yet, the Platonic Representation Hypothesis suggests that models trained on different modalities may converge spontaneously toward a shared representation geometry. But then, do we even need paired examples for cross-modal alignment? Remarkably, we show that paired examples are unnecessary for coarse cross-modal alignment. Our simple Wasserstein Procrustes method with a coarse geometric initialization aligns two disjoint embedding sets by estimating a single orthogonal map without seeing any pairs. Across datasets, modalities, and unimodal models, we show that we can consistently align independently trained representations without pairs, and standard geometric alignment metrics accurately predict when this is possible. Nevertheless, we can naturally benefit from paired examples. In the very few-pair regime, our method substantially outperforms existing ones, while staying competitive with pair-based methods with more added examples. Finally, we demonstrate that the resulting alignments can enable text-to-image generation without paired examples. These results show that independently trained models often share enough geometry to establish cross-modal correspondence with little or no paired data.
